While it is not possible to definitively distinguish between common source vs. lateral transfer, common source is somewhat more probable. The properties border each other, but did not share equipment. Both premises have ponds, domestic birds are allowed to free-range, and wild waterfowl move back and forth between these properties. The genomic information indicates that the virus samples from these premises are almost identical. Additionally the birds developed clinical signs on these properties on the same day. While lateral transfer could lead to contemporaneous development of clinical signs given the variability in the prepatent period and incubation period, a more likely scenario is that the birds on both premises had a common source exposure at approximately the same time
